rendered: Prodigiosin production peaks at peaking at 25–28 ◦C and suppressed at ≥37 ◦C[1]. The pigmentation contrast is shown in Fig. 2[2] (panel A), where the plate kept at 25-28 °C[3] shows red/pink pigmented colonies and the plate at ≥37 °C[4] shows pale cream colonies with no visible red pigment. The document also gives a mechanism: prodigiosin production is temperature-dependent because of decreased expression and stability of PigF and PigN at higher[5] temperatures.
